do.name: Teatro Olimpico
do.detail: Opened in 1585 and the oldest surviving indoor theatre anywhere. Palladio's last design, finished after his death by Scamozzi, who built the trompe l'oeil streets receding behind the stage.

do.name: Villa La Rotonda
do.detail: Begun in 1567 on a low hill outside town: four identical porticoed fronts around a domed hall, the building copied more than any other in Europe. Opening is limited, largely weekends, so check before going.

do.name: Basilica Palladiana and Piazza dei Signori
do.detail: White marble loggias wrap the old town hall, and the terrace above looks over the square and its tower.

do.name: Climb the portico to Monte Berico
do.detail: A covered arcaded ramp of many arches climbs from town to the sanctuary and the view back over the roofs.

do.name: Walk the Palladian route along Corso Palladio
do.detail: One straight street strings together the palaces he built, shops and cafes filling the ground floors.

do.name: Santa Corona
do.detail: A brick Gothic church holding Bellini and Veronese paintings, and the tomb of Palladio himself.

do.name: Baccala alla vicentina and a Colli Berici wine
do.detail: Salt cod stewed slowly with milk and onion is the city dish, poured alongside wines from the hills south.

do.name: Palazzo Chiericati
do.detail: Another Palladio front, now the city art gallery, with northern Italian painting inside.
